text:
sre-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT PAGE — severity P1 — elevated 5xx rate on /api/v1/users during canary rollout of release/2026-03-db-schema

oncall-jo: I’m on it. Paging the release owner and infra. Can everyone move to this thread pls.

deploy-bot: Canary progress: 2/5 canaries failed (instances in eu-west-1). Fail reason: application SQL errors. Rolling pause initiated automatically.

lara: Saw spikes in DB error logs — looks like migrations ran with the new service deploy. Error: "null value in column \"prefs\" violates not-null constraint" for insert into users.

oncall-jo: Did the migration add a NOT NULL column? That would be breaking.

dmitri: Yes — migration migrate_2026_03_add_user_prefs added users.prefs jsonb NOT NULL with no default. It should have been nullable + backfilled. The deploy ran before backfill completed on a small shard.

lara: Repro from canary instance:
```
org.redwood.api.UserService - INSERT INTO users (id, email, prefs) VALUES ($1,$2,$3) -> ERROR: null value in column \"prefs\" violates not-null constraint
Stack: java.sql.BatchUpdateException: ERROR: null value in column \"prefs\" violates not-null constraint
```

oncall-jo: Ok. Immediate mitigation options: 1) Kill feature flag for new_user_flow (fast) 2) Rollback service to previous version (slower but migration-safe) 3) Run emergency backfill/migration to add default value (risky during traffic). Thoughts?

dmitri: We should kill the FF first. If old code path avoids writing prefs, that should stop new errors. Rolling back while migrations are non-idempotent is risky.

deploy-bot: Feature flag endpoint: FF:new_user_flow - current state: enabled for canary group. API: POST /flags/new_user_flow/disable {"scope":"canary"}

oncall-jo: Doing FF kill now.

oncall-jo: @deploy-bot disable new_user_flow for canary -> ✅

sre-bot: ACTION LOG — 1768501248 — oncall-jo disabled FF:new_user_flow for canary

lara: After FF kill, error rate dropped ~70% on canary instances but DB still shows migration lock in progress on one leader node.

rohan: I’m seeing a stuck migration job on db-primary: process id 12823 holding SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE lock on table users. Backfill attempted by migration worker but got blocked and timed out.

dmitri: Can you paste output of 
```
SELECT pid, state, query, wait_event_type, wait_event FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE query LIKE '%migrate_2026_03_add_user_prefs%';
```

rohan: Output:
```
 pid | state  | query                                         | wait_event_type | wait_event
-----+--------+-----------------------------------------------+-----------------+-----------
12823| active | UPDATE users SET prefs = '{}' WHERE prefs IS NULL | Lock            | ShareUpdateExclusiveLock
12824| idle   | ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN prefs jsonb NOT NULL | Idle            |           
```

oncall-jo: Looks like ALTER TABLE completed but UPDATE backfill is stuck due to lock by another long-running statement. That UPDATE is the backfill itself — weird. Could be a transaction that didn't commit.

dmitri: We need to free that lock. Options: kill pid 12823 to allow ALTER to finish/commit, or cancel backfill transaction gracefully. Killing may cause partial updates. Given customer impact, I recommend: 1) keep FF killed, 2) cancel/kill the backfill PID to unblock, 3) rollback deploy to be safe, then schedule safe backfill on a maintenance window.

oncall-jo: I will cancel pid 12823 now. @rohan please confirm you can repro and observe.

rohan: Cancel sent -> "canceling statement due to user request". Lock released. ALTER shows completed.

lara: Good — 5xx rate dropped to baseline after FF kill + cancel. But we still have canary instances with older binary expecting prefs non-null; there are some queued failed requests.

customer-support: Notifying customers impacted: we have two enterprise tenants reported errors (ACME Corp and Nimbus Labs). Escalating to CS lead.

oncall-jo: OK. Next steps: 1) abort/rollback the current rollout to prevent reintroducing bad code 2) create a mitigation ticket to convert migration to safe pattern (nullable -> backfill -> set not-null -> remove default) 3) plan customer communication.

dmitri: I will prepare the rollback command. Note: ensure we do NOT run migrations on rollback path. Use deploy tag release/2026-03-db-schema@previous without running migrations.

deploy-bot: Rollback initiated: reverting service image to release/2026-02-stable across canary -> batch -> global. Estimated time: 7m per batch.

oncall-jo: During rollback we should watch DB error rate. If it spikes, we might need to cut traffic (route to read-only).

lara: Also adding temporary DB trigger to coerce inserts that lack prefs to '{}', to stop errors while rollback finishes. Patch SQL: 
```
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION ensure_prefs() RETURNS trigger AS $$
BEGIN
  IF NEW.prefs IS NULL THEN
    NEW.prefs = '{}';
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
CREATE TRIGGER ensure_prefs_before_insert BEFORE INSERT ON users FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION ensure_prefs();
```

rohan: Deployed trigger on read-write nodes. This should be transient — will disable after rollback completes.

deploy-bot: Rollback progress: batch 1 complete, batch 2 in progress.

oncall-jo: Handing over to night oncall @dmitri in 30m. If rollback completes and errors are stable, we declare mitigation. If not, escalate to infra lead.

dmitri: Acknowledged handoff. I will monitor and update status. Preparing follow-up PR to change migration to nullable + bg backfill + set not null with timeout.

customer-support: I’ve opened ticket CS-9821 for ACME and CS-9822 for Nimbus with interim workaround notes and ETA for full resolution.

sre-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — 1768503600 — mitigation in place: feature flag kill, DB trigger applied, rollback in progress. Customer impact: degraded for canary traffic only; two enterprise customers reported errors; CS tickets created.

oncall-jo: Thanks everyone. Final note: owners for postmortem: dmitri (migration), lara (app change), rohan (db ops), oncall-jo (incident lead). I’ll set severity: P1 -> reduced to P2 after rollback confirmed.

dmitri: Will draft postmortem and broken down action items.

rohan: Disabling the temporary trigger now that rollback completed and error rate steady. Will keep audit logs.

sre-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — 1768504678 — rollback complete, DB stable, feature flag remains disabled pending safe migration rollout. Postmortem assigned. :white_check_mark:
